title: Handler comment claims no stamp-without-send can survive the transaction, but clear_rejected_stamps swallows clear failures and the transaction still commits
evidence:
+              // fails send-time validation — all before commit, so no crash
+              // window can leave a stamp-without-send behind. | +    case clear(db, vacancy_uuid, addr) {
+      Error(db_err) ->
+        wisp.log_error(
+          "invalid-sender stamp clear failed for "
detail: A failed in-transaction clear is logged, not propagated; clear_rejected_stamps returns Nil and the transaction returns Ok, committing the stamp. The 'failure anywhere rolls both marks back' guarantee does not hold for clear errors.
recommended_fix: Either propagate clear errors to roll back the transaction, or soften the comment to state that clear failures are logged and the stamp may persist.

title: Submit latch is set on the submit event even if form.js's client-side preflight cancels the POST, permanently suppressing the abandoned event for that pageview
detail: form.js loads first and performs a preflight; if it preventDefaults, the submission never happens but submitted stays true (reset only on bfcache pageshow), so onHidden/onPagehide are suppressed for a user who never actually submitted.
recommended_fix: Re-arm the latch when the page does not unload (e.g. reset submitted on the next input/change event, or hook preflight failure) so blocked submits don't mute abandonment tracking.
